commands = ["root", "init", "index", "new", "list", "graph", "edit", "tag", "tag_list"]
for cmd in commands:
    with open(f"mock_help/{cmd}.txt") as f:
        text = f.read()
    
    flags = set()
    in_flags = False
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        if line.startswith("Flags:"):
            in_flags = True
            continue
        if in_flags:
            if not line.startswith(" ") and line.strip() != "" and not line.startswith("Formatting") and not line.startswith("Filtering") and not line.startswith("Sorting"):
                # might be end of flags section, but let's just parse all lines
                pass
            
            # Find all flags like -h, --help, --notebook-dir
            # We look at the first part of the line before multiple spaces
            parts = line.split("  ")
            if len(parts) > 1:
                flag_part = parts[1].strip()
                if flag_part.startswith("-"):
                    # Extract individual flags, e.g., "-h, --help"
                    for chunk in flag_part.split(","):
                        chunk = chunk.strip().split("=")[0]
                        if chunk.startswith("-"):
                            flags.add(chunk)
            
            # Also just run a regex on the whole line to be safe, looking for --[a-z-]+ and -[a-zA-Z]
            # but only before the description
            desc_start = line.find("    ")
            if desc_start != -1:
                flag_str = line[:desc_start]
                for m in re.findall(r'--[a-zA-Z0-9-]+|-[a-zA-Z0-9]', flag_str):
                    flags.add(m)
                    
    print(f"{cmd}: {sorted(list(flags))}")
